transcript.text: My Hotpoint washer dryer isn't drying properly any more and there's a funny smell when it's on the dry bit. Is there something I should clean?

Yes, please start by cleaning the lint filter at the bottom front of the machine and checking the condenser if your model has one. That funny smell is often caused by fluff or lint getting trapped near the heating element because airflow is restricted. It could also be that you are drying a load that is too large for the dry cycle, as washer-dryers handle much less laundry when drying than washing. Please switch off and unplug the appliance before attempting any cleaning to keep it safe. Let me know if the smell persists after you have cleared out the filter and condenser.

Ok thanks. The smell is like burning dust, a bit scorched, and the top of the machine gets really hot when it's drying. I've carried on using it though. Where exactly is the filter, I didn't know it needed cleaning?

⚠ Stop using this appliance
A burning or hot-plastic smell, smoke, scorching or melting can mean an electrical fault or a fire risk. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it (or turn it off at the fuse box), and don't run it again — not even as a test — until it has been checked by a qualified engineer. The filter is located behind a small door at the bottom front of the machine. Given the burning dust smell and excessive heat, it sounds like lint or debris may be scorching on the heating element due to restricted airflow. However, because this indicates a potential fire hazard, you must stop using the appliance immediately until a qualified engineer has checked it. While waiting for the engineer, please ensure the machine is switched off and unplugged.
